Saturn glows with more heat than sunlight gives it.
Saturn dumps 2.5 times more heat into space.

title: Saturn Glows With Its Own Internal Rain
description: Saturn radiates 2.5 times more energy into space than it receives from the Sun. Liquid helium raining through hydrogen produces massive friction heat at its core.

beats.text: Saturn radiates 2.5 times more energy than it receives.
beats.visual: Full view photograph of Saturn and its ring system taken by Cassini, 2004

beats.text: Most people think distant planets are warmed only by sunlight.
beats.visual: Illustration of the outer solar system showing distant sunlight hitting Saturn, 2021

beats.text: Deep inside, Saturn's core burns at 11,700 degrees Celsius.
beats.visual: Diagram showing the internal core structure and atmosphere of Saturn, 2017

beats.text: Helium condenses high in the hydrogen atmosphere and rains downward.
beats.visual: Artist depiction of liquid helium droplets descending through Saturn mantle, 2018
queries: Gas giant liquid helium mantle concept

beats.text: Friction from falling liquid helium creates massive internal heat.
beats.visual: Cutaway graphic of friction heating in Saturn interior atmosphere, 2019

beats.text: This heat engine powers winds reaching 1,800 kilometers per hour.
beats.visual: Cassini spacecraft image of fast cloud bands in Saturn upper atmosphere, 2008

beats.text: The heat even drives a giant hexagonal storm at its north pole.
beats.visual: Cassini image of the giant hexagonal cloud pattern at Saturn north pole, 2013

beats.text: That internal engine is why Saturn radiates 2.5 times more energy than it receives.
beats.visual: Wide backlighted view of Saturn and its ring system captured by Cassini, 2006

better_than_last: Replaced technical orbital and density calculations with direct internal energy and atmospheric wind comparisons to improve retention.
